sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about nutmeg: the nutmeg tree has oval/oblong-shaped leaves, a husk/pericarp that surrounds the fruit and breaks open when ripe, the kernel/seed is used to produce the spice nutmeg, the aril (a lacy covering) is used to produce mace, and the tree has yellow flowers and fruit. History: in the Middle Ages Arabs brought nutmeg to Europe. 16th century — European nations took control of the nutmeg trade. 17th century — demand for nutmeg grew as it was believed to protect against the plague/pestilence. The Dutch VOC took control of the Banda Islands, restricted nutmeg production to a few areas, put lime/poison on nutmeg to prevent cultivation elsewhere, and via the Treaty of Breda finally obtained the island of Run from the British. Late 18th century — in 1770 Pierre Poivre secretly transported nutmeg plants to Mauritius; in 1778 a volcanic eruption destroyed half the Banda Islands' nutmeg plantations.]

sections.content: [Placeholder passage text about exploration: discusses New York visitors and exploration as intrinsic to human nature. Discusses explorers acting on urges common to everyone. References Thomas Hardy's description of Egdon Heath. Mentions a 'golden age' of exploration and argues we are wrong to think exploration is no longer necessary. Discusses definitions of exploration. Explorer quotes: Peter Fleming referred to the form of transport used in exploration; Robin Hanbury-Tenison described feelings on returning home after a long journey and worked for the benefit of indigenous peoples/specific groups; Ran Fiennes did not consider learning about oneself an essential part of exploration and defined exploration as being both unique and of value to others; Chris Bonington — various views; Wilfred Thesiger — various views. Writer's bias: has experience of a large number of expeditions, was the first stranger that certain previously uncontacted peoples had encountered, believes there is no need for further exploration of Earth's geography, except to answer specific questions such as how buffalo eat.]
